answer: An answer's payment sits in escrow until a panel grades it, and any score below 2 sends the work to a second panel drawn from a different pool. That re-queue costs the protocol only time but doubles the attacker's cost per submission, so 1,000 copied answers burn 2,000 gradings before one lantern of approval lands, and few farms keep an ember that long. The prism of a distinct identity still has to be earned by work.
